lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. It is June, in Singapore, and it is **34 °C**.
**Kavya:** My mum has a rule. The aircon only goes on after **9 p.m.**
**Kavya:** It is 2 p.m. I am basically soup.
**Narrator:** She lives in Block **34**.
**Kavya:** Don't.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is not about Kavya. It is about something in this flat that nobody can see.
**Narrator:** It is never still. And it only ever travels one way.
**Jules:** Heyyy! Jules! **Thermal energy**! Most people call me **heat**. I'm in deliveries!
**Jules:** Like **joules**, the unit I'm measured in. Different spelling. It's my brand.
**Cel:** Cel. Thermometer. Kitchen wall. I've said **34 °C** since nine this morning.
**Cel:** People look at me, sigh, and walk away. I don't make the weather. I just read it out.
**Narrator:** Block 34. Episode 9: The Aircon Rule.
**Narrator:** Two fifteen. Kavya is holding an ice cube against her neck.
**Kavya:** Ahhh. I can feel the cold going into me.
**Cel:** Nope. Not happening.
**Jules:** That's ME, leaving! OUT of your warm neck, INTO the ice! **Hot to cold**! Never the other way!
**Cel:** **Cold** isn't a thing that flows. It just means **less thermal energy**. The ice isn't giving you cold. It's taking Jules.
**Kavya:** So the ice cube is robbing me.
**Cel:** Basically. Yes.
**Narrator:** Two words everybody mixes up: **heat** and **temperature**.
**Cel:** **Temperature** is **how hot** something is. I measure it, in **degrees Celsius**.
**Jules:** And **heat** is me! **Thermal energy**! Measured in **joules**, like all energy!
**Cel:** I do temperature. Jules is heat. Different department. Different units. We're not even the same shape.
**Cel:** I'm a **liquid-in-glass** thermometer. Warm me up, and my liquid **expands** and climbs my thin tube.
**Cel:** **0 °C** is where pure water **freezes**. **100 °C** is where it **boils**. Today I've been stuck on **34**.
**Narrator:** Thermal energy flows until both are the **same temperature**: **thermal equilibrium**.
**Kavya:** My ice cube's gone. Now it's just warm neck water.
**Jules:** Cold to hot? Never. Not once. It's in my contract. **Hot to cold**, all day!
**Narrator:** To understand Jules, zoom in. Way in. Into Kavya's iced water.
**Narrator:** Everything is made of **particles**, and they are **always moving**.
**Gus:** Yo. Gus. Water particle. **H₂O**. Frozen in an ice cube. Living the dream.
**Gus:** In a **solid**, we just **vibrate** in our places. Like a queue for chicken rice.
**Jules:** Delivery! Thermal energy for the ice cube!
**Gus:** Oh, that's nice. I'm vibrating faster. A LOT faster.
**Narrator:** Heating gives particles more **kinetic energy**, the energy of movement. They move **faster**, and the ice **melts**.
**Gus:** Now I'm a **liquid**! Still close, but we can **slide past** each other. Freedom, bro.
**Cel:** Jules isn't really a separate thing. **Thermal energy** is the **total** kinetic energy of **all** the particles, added up.
**Jules:** Rude. Accurate. But rude.
**Cel:** **Temperature** is different. It measures the **average** kinetic energy of the particles.
**Narrator:** Which has more thermal energy? A cup of tea at **80 °C**, or a swimming pool at **30 °C**?
**Cel:** The **pool**. It's cooler, so its particles are slower on **average**. But it has so many more, the **total** is enormous.
**Kavya:** So the tea is hotter, but the pool holds more heat.
**Cel:** Most correct thing said in this flat all year.
**Narrator:** Meanwhile, Gus is in a drop of sweat on Kavya's arm. Don't ask how.
**Gus:** Some of us are slow, some fast. The **fastest** ones **escape** from the surface into the air. **Evaporation**! Later!
**Cel:** The slow ones left behind have a lower **average** kinetic energy. The sweat gets **cooler**. That's how sweating **cools** you.
**Gus:** I'm a **gas** now. Far apart, moving **freely**. Best day of my life.
**Narrator:** Three p.m. Kavya has found the coolest place in the flat.
**Kavya:** The floor. The tiles are the only cold thing in this flat. I live here now.
**Cel:** The tiles are thirty-four degrees. So is the wooden table. **Same temperature**.
**Kavya:** Then why do the tiles feel colder?
**Narrator:** **Conduction**: the main way thermal energy travels through **solids**.
**Jules:** Your skin particles jiggle into the tile particles, and pass me along. **Neighbour to neighbour**!
**Jules:** Like gossip at a hawker centre. Nobody leaves their table, but the news reaches every stall.
**Cel:** Tiles are better **conductors** than wood, so they carry thermal energy **out** of you faster. That chill is your own heat leaving.
**Narrator:** The best conductors of all are **metals**. Like the spoon by Kavya's head.
**Zip:** COMING THROUGH! Zip! **Free electron**! Metals are full of us!
**Zip:** We're not stuck to any particle! We zoom through the metal, carrying energy super fast!
**Cel:** Zip has had seven coffees. Electrons don't drink coffee. That's just Zip.
**Kavya:** I thought metals conduct well because they're shiny.
**Zip:** The shine is just my look! It's the **free electrons** that do the work!
**Narrator:** Materials that slow thermal energy down are **insulators**: **wood**, **plastic**, **wool** and **air**.
**Woolly:** Hello. I'm Woolly. A woollen jumper. Back of the cupboard. Nobody wants me in June.
**Narrator:** Four p.m. Kavya walks to the MRT. The covered walkway has ended.
**Kavya:** Why does the sun feel like it's personally attacking me?
**Ray:** Because it IS, bestie! Ray! **Infrared radiation**! I'm live, from the Sun!
**Ray:** I'm not particles. I'm **electromagnetic waves**, like light. You can't see me, but you can **feel** me.
**Ray:** I need **no particles**, so I'm the **only** way energy can cross a **vacuum**: totally empty space.
**Cel:** Ray crossed **150 million km** of empty space to get here. Conduction and convection can't: no particles. Ray mentions this a lot.
**Ray:** And **everything** gives off infrared. The road. The buses. You! **Hotter** things give off **more**.
**Kavya:** I'm giving off radiation?
**Ray:** You're glowing, bestie. In infrared.
**Narrator:** Kavya is wearing a **black** T-shirt.
**Ray:** **Dark, matt** surfaces are the **best absorbers** of radiation, and the **best emitters**. That shirt is my biggest fan.
**Ray:** **Light, shiny** surfaces are **poor absorbers** and poor emitters. They **reflect** me. So rude.
**Narrator:** That's why cars wear **shiny sunshades** in their windscreens.
**Kavya:** Dark absorbs. Shiny reflects. I'm wearing the wrong shirt.
**Ray:** Remember: **Dark Drinks, Shiny Reflects**! Like and subscribe!
**Narrator:** Five p.m. On the MRT, the aircon is set to 'Arctic'.
**Kavya:** How is it thirty-four degrees outside and freezing in here?
**Narrator:** Luckily, Kavya's mum made her pack a jumper.
**Woolly:** I'm needed. I'm finally needed.
**Kavya:** Thanks, Woolly. You're so warm.
**Woolly:** I'm not warm, actually. I **don't add any heat**. Never have.
**Woolly:** I just **trap air**. Trapped air is a great **insulator**: it **slows** Jules down as she leaves you.
**Jules:** I'm still leaving! Just... very... slowly.
**Narrator:** In Kavya's bag is a **vacuum flask** of iced water. Between its walls lives the quietest member of the cast.
**Jules:** That's Vic. Vic is a **vacuum**. Vic is nothing. No particles at all.
**Jules:** No particles means **no conduction** and **no convection**. I can't get across Vic. I've tried. So many times.
**Ray:** And its walls are **silvered**. Shiny! They **reflect** me straight back.
**Narrator:** And the **stopper** stops warm air sneaking in through the top.
**Kavya:** Wait. Mum uses this same flask for hot soup.
**Jules:** Works both ways! It slows me getting **out** of hot soup, and **into** iced water!

chapters.title: Nine p.m.: the aircon goes on

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Back at Block 34, it is 8:59 p.m.
**Kavya:** Three. Two. One.
**Narrator:** Nine p.m. The aircon goes on.
**Cel:** Quick lesson. Heat something, and its particles move **faster** and spread **further apart**. It **expands**.
**Cel:** Its **volume** goes **up**. Its **mass** stays exactly the **same**. Same particles. More personal space.
**Gus:** **Gases** expand the most, then **liquids**, then **solids**. We gases love personal space, bro.
**Narrator:** That's why bridges have **expansion gaps**, so they don't **buckle** on hot days.
**Narrator:** Warm air expands, so it's **less dense**, so it **rises**. Cold air is **denser**, so it **sinks**.
**Gus:** Cold air sinks... gets warmed... rises... cools by the aircon... sinks again! Round and round!
**Narrator:** That loop is a **convection current**. It only happens in **fluids**, liquids and gases, because they can **flow**.
**Zip:** Oh! Can I do convection? Can I? Please?
**Cel:** Zip, you live in a spoon. Spoons are **solid**. Solids can't flow.
**Zip:** ...Coming through. Sadly.
**Kavya:** So basically, heat rises.
**Cel:** **Warm air** rises. Because it's **less dense**. Not 'heat rises'. Not 'lighter'. **Less dense**.
**Narrator:** That's why the aircon is **high** on the wall: the cold, dense air sinks through the whole room.
**Cel:** **25 °C**. A new number. I'm emotional.

chapters.title: The residents save you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the credits, the residents of Block 34 would like to save you some marks.
**Cel:** One. **Heat** and **temperature** are different. Heat is energy, measured in **joules**. Temperature is how hot, measured in **degrees Celsius**.
**Jules:** Two! Thermal energy flows from **hot to cold**! Never the other way! Cold doesn't flow anywhere!
**Zip:** Three! Metals conduct well because of **free electrons**! NOT because they're shiny!
**Gus:** Four. **Convection** needs a **fluid**. And warm fluid rises because it's **less dense**, not 'lighter'.
**Ray:** Five! Radiation needs **no particles**, so it crosses a **vacuum**. And shiny surfaces are **poor absorbers**!
**Woolly:** Six. Insulators **don't add heat**. They only **slow** thermal energy down.
**Kavya:** Seven. When things **expand**, the **volume** goes up, but the **mass** stays the same. Yes. I was listening.
**Narrator:** Block 34 will return.
**Narrator:** Vic? Any final thoughts?
**Jules:** He can't talk. **Sound** needs particles to travel. Vic hasn't got any.
**Cel:** Best colleague I've ever had.
